name: AI-native software
tagline: Narrow fresher door, but the only software door that is growing in 2026

door_size.caveat: FirstMeridian projection of 1 lakh entry-level GCC jobs over 2025 to 2030 spread evenly; only about 10,000 entry-level tech openings were live in May 2026 (Xpheno), and freshers were 15% of GCC hiring in 2025, down from 28%.

pay_band.note: GCC 8 to 12 and product companies 8 to 15 for most; AI/ML roles at funded startups 18 to 25 and a few big-tech new-grad offers above 30 go to a very small number, mostly from tier-1 campuses. Source is a low-confidence salary guide.

tiers_realistic.tier1: Yes. GCCs, product companies and AI startups still run campus drives at IITs, NITs, IIITs and BITS, but even there 38% of the 2024 IIT batch was unplaced (supply.iit.unplaced_share.2024), so the brand alone no longer closes the offer.
tiers_realistic.tier2: Yes, with a portfolio. Off-campus drives (Amazon SDE-1, Fractal Imagineers, Mu Sigma, Zoho, Flipkart GRiD) accept any college; a 7+ CGPA filter and an online coding test are the first gates, then the shipped project decides.
tiers_realistic.tier3: Possible but the minority outcome; expect 12 to 18 months of building before the first offer. What substitutes for the brand: a deployed, working AI application in a real domain with a public repo and a written evaluation, plus one open-source contribution or a paid freelance build. Only 6 in 100 tech postings were entry-level in mid-2026 (demand.prepnplaced.entry_level_posting_share.2026), so apply through hackathons, hiring challenges and referrals, not job boards alone. Employability for AI/ML roles among graduates tested was 46% (supply.mettl2025.employability.ai_ml_roles): most applicants fail the basics, so basics done properly are a real edge.

entry_requirements: Python with the standard data stack (pandas, FastAPI or Flask) and SQL: every online test and take-home starts here
Data structures and algorithms at LeetCode easy-to-medium level; still the first screen at Amazon, Flipkart, Razorpay, Zoho
One deployed project that calls an LLM API, uses retrieval (RAG), has written evals and is visible on GitHub with a README a recruiter can run
One cloud (AWS, Azure or GCP) at free-tier level: deploy a container, set up a queue, read logs, know what a bill looks like
Git, Docker, basic Linux and CI (GitHub Actions); GCC interviews ask how you shipped, not just what you built
Ability to explain a system you built for 30 minutes, including what broke and how you tested it; interviewers now assume the code was AI-assisted and probe understanding
7+ CGPA and no active backlogs for most GCC and analytics trainee filters (Fractal Imagineers screens on both)

two_year_plan.title: Foundations: Python, SQL, DSA, one cloud
learn: Python properly: NPTEL 'Programming, Data Structures and Algorithms using Python' (free), then Harvard CS50P (free)
SQL on a real dataset: SQLBolt then Mode SQL tutorial; practice joins, window functions, indexes on PostgreSQL
DSA: 150 LeetCode problems (arrays, strings, hashing, trees, graphs, DP basics) at 1 to 2 a day
Git and GitHub, Linux shell, Docker basics via the free Docker curriculum
AWS Cloud Practitioner material (free digital training) or Microsoft Learn AZ-900; FutureSkills Prime cloud pathway if you want a government-recognised certificate at no cost
build: A CLI or small web app (FastAPI) that reads and writes a PostgreSQL database, deployed on Render, Railway or AWS free tier
A public GitHub profile with weekly commits; README for every repo
target: TCS NQT, Infosys, Cognizant GenC as fallback registrations
Flipkart GRiD if in third year

two_year_plan.title: Build with LLM APIs, RAG and evals
learn: Calling LLM APIs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, or open models via Ollama and Hugging Face): prompts, structured outputs, tool calling, streaming, cost and token maths
Retrieval-augmented generation: chunking, embeddings, pgvector or Chroma, hybrid search, re-ranking
Evals: build a 50-question test set for your app, score it automatically, track regressions; read the OpenAI and Anthropic eval cookbooks
Agent frameworks at a working level (LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, or CrewAI); understand what they do so you can also build without them
Observability: log every prompt, latency and cost; use Langfuse (open-source) or OpenTelemetry
build: The evidenced project below: an agentic assistant over real domain documents with retrieval, evals and a cost dashboard
A second, smaller build: a data pipeline (Airflow or Prefect, free) that loads a public dataset into a warehouse (DuckDB or BigQuery sandbox) and refreshes daily
evidence: Eval results table in the README
Blog post on one hard bug
target: Fractal Imagineers, Mu Sigma trainee decision scientist
Internship applications at GCCs (Sparkplug-style programmes if your college is on the list)

two_year_plan.title: Production skills and a domain
learn: System design for freshers: queues, caching, idempotency, retries, rate limits; design one service end to end on paper
Testing and CI: pytest, GitHub Actions, contract tests for your API
Kubernetes basics (minikube) and infrastructure as code (Terraform free tier) for platform and MLOps roles
Security basics: OWASP top 10, secrets management, prompt-injection defences for LLM apps
Pick one domain (banking, insurance, logistics, healthcare, retail, telecom) and learn its vocabulary and its regulator's rules; GCCs hire into domains
build: Harden the H2 project: auth, rate limiting, CI, a load test, a runbook
One open-source contribution (a bug fix or docs PR to LangGraph, Langfuse, FastAPI or a similar project)
evidence: Architecture diagram and runbook in the repo
target: Amazon SDE-1 off-campus, Razorpay, Flipkart, Zoho
GCC early-careers pages (Goldman Sachs, Deloitte USI, Walmart Global Tech)

two_year_plan.title: Interviews, referrals and the first offer
learn: Revise DSA to 250 solved with mock interviews (Pramp, peers); GCC rounds are 3 to 4 technical interviews plus a values round
Behavioural stories: five projects framed as problem, action, measured result
Salary negotiation basics and how to read a CTC breakup (fixed vs variable vs joining bonus)
build: A one-page portfolio site listing the three builds with links and eval numbers
Weekly applications: 10 targeted, referral-first, tracked in a sheet; message alumni on LinkedIn with the demo link, not a CV
evidence: Interview log with what failed and what was fixed
target: Any GCC, product company or AI startup with an entry or junior posting
Fallback: it_services specialist tracks (Infosys DSE, TCS Digital) which pay above the mass-recruiter band

evidenced_project_spec.title: Claims copilot for a general insurer
evidenced_project_spec.scope: An assistant that ingests 200 to 500 anonymised or synthetic motor-insurance claim documents (FIR, surveyor report, policy PDF, garage invoice), answers a claims officer's questions with citations, flags missing documents against the policy's checklist, and drafts the settlement note. Includes retrieval over the documents, a tool that reads the policy schedule, an eval set of 60 questions with expected answers, and a dashboard of cost, latency and accuracy per release.
evidenced_project_spec.agent_use: A coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, or an open-source equivalent) scaffolds the FastAPI service, writes the first tests and generates synthetic claim files; the graduate reviews every diff, writes the retrieval and eval logic by hand, and keeps a log of what the agent got wrong. A research agent is used to summarise IRDAI motor-claim timelines, which the graduate then verifies against the regulator's page.
evidenced_project_spec.done_looks_like: Deployed at a public URL with login; answers 60-question eval at 85% or better with citations; flags missing documents correctly on 20 held-out claims; total cost per claim under Rs 5; README explains architecture, eval method, failure cases and what is not automated (final settlement decision stays with the officer).
evidenced_project_spec.verification: Automated eval run in CI on every commit with results committed to the repo; a 3-minute demo video; one insurance professional or faculty member reviews five outputs and their comments are in the repo; a 30-minute walkthrough the graduate can give without notes covering chunking choices, one hallucination they caught and how the eval set was built.

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Write CRUD endpoints, boilerplate and unit tests by hand
ai_task_shift.now: Coding agents generate most boilerplate and first-draft tests; a fresher who only does this has no edge
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Specifying the behaviour precisely, reviewing generated code for correctness and security, and owning what ships

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Read documentation and Stack Overflow to learn a new library
ai_task_shift.now: Agents explain and integrate libraries on demand
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Judging which tool fits, what the trade-offs are, and knowing enough fundamentals to catch a wrong answer

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Manual testing and bug triage on a ticket queue (the classic fresher job)
ai_task_shift.now: Agents write regression tests, reproduce bugs and propose fixes; this entry-level rung is shrinking fastest
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Designing evals and test strategy, deciding what 'correct' means for the business, and debugging the cases agents cannot reproduce

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Build dashboards and reports in SQL and Excel for analysts
ai_task_shift.now: Text-to-SQL and agentic analytics produce first drafts
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Data modelling, checking the numbers against the source of truth, and explaining them to the business

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Deploy and monitor a service by following a runbook
ai_task_shift.now: Agents execute runbooks and draft incident summaries
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Architecture, cost control, reliability targets and the judgement call during an incident

ai_task_shift.task_2019: Not a fresher task: building AI features
ai_task_shift.now: Every product team is adding LLM features; building, evaluating and running them is the new entry-level work, and AI/ML postings grew 31% year on year in Aug 2026 (demand.naukri.jobspeak.ai_ml_yoy.aug2026)
ai_task_shift.human_owns: Product sense for what the model should and should not do, evaluation, guardrails, and observability

fit_rules.reason: CS is what most GCC and product filters ask for, and your syllabus already covers DSA and databases.
IT degrees pass the same filters as CS for software and data roles.
ECE graduates are accepted by most software drives (Fractal lists ECE) but must self-teach DSA and databases.
Few software drives accept Civil; you would compete against CS graduates with no syllabus support.
Campus drives from GCCs and product companies still come to tier-1 colleges.
Almost no AI-native employer visits tier-3 campuses; you enter through off-campus drives and a portfolio, which takes longer.
These jobs are concentrated in Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Pune, Chennai and NCR.
Unless home is one of six metros, there are almost no AI-native fresher jobs near home; remote fresher roles are rare.
Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Chennai hold most GCC and AI startup seats.
The first offer on this path usually takes 12 to 18 months of building for a tier-2/3 graduate; with no runway, take an IT services or apprenticeship job and build on the side.
A year of runway is enough to build the portfolio this path needs.
This path is building software every day.
Data engineering, analytics trainee and evaluation work are large parts of this path.
Little of this path touches machines or structures; consider ev_automotive or semiconductor if that is what you like.
Fresher pay here is two to four times the IT services band, with faster growth, at the cost of a harder entry.
This is the slowest path to a first salary for most tier-2/3 graduates.
A shipped project is the single strongest signal on this path.
DSA is still the first screen at Amazon, Flipkart, Razorpay and most GCCs.
Starting from zero, plan for the full two-year timeline before expecting offers here.
You already like the daily work of this path.
